# Capwise logarithmic defect flux and exclusion on uniformly proper source sections

This refines the full-body defect identity from `candidate d9362f528596f345`. The new invariant retains an actual cap's body selector, its cap-restricted tilted-volume defect, and a possibly nonzero logarithmic SECTION defect. The latter vanishes on uniformly interior source sections but cannot be discarded on arbitrary other fibers.

No defect exclusion or Gamma payment follows. The two explicit triangle calibrations below show why the extra section term is necessary.

## 1. Actual sequence and joint cap records

Use the fixed-base, positive-body, finite-plane, uniformly bounded-source setup of `candidate 8ba63f3af7e6943f`. In particular, after a subsequence,

    L_j -> L=min_i A_i uniformly on a common compact set,
    nu_j=dm_j/(M_j L_j) -> dm/(M L)+zeta,
    zeta=sum_i zeta_i,
    grad_X log L_j dm_j -> grad_X log L dm+M sum_i c_i zeta_i.

The whole surface-log defect b is recorded on the actual normal bundle:

    (-log L_j)_+ eta_j -> (-log L)_+ eta+b,
    -pi_*(n b)=M sum_i c_i zeta_i.                    (1)

All these are the same actual source labels and measures. The limiting zero set Z={L=0} has continuous codimension at least two in each sampled fiber.

Retain one sequence of actual cap records

    H_j={a_j.z+u_j.X>=t_j},   (a_j,u_j,t_j)->(a,u,t),
    |u_j|>=b_*>0.

An auxiliary trace-preserving bounded representative is permitted, but no claim about replacing its global covering resultant is needed here. Let s_j be its actual consistent body selector and lambda_j its actual allocated coarea measure. Assume their joint limits are the consistent limiting selector s and allocated section measure lambda supplied by the cap-record compactification theorem. Proper sections are fully counted; inside/outside supporting allocations obey body+section=1 and body=section, respectively.

Write H for the limiting cap. We first prove the formulas for one record; finitely many fixed labeled records and convergent weights can then be summed. No arbitrary unrecorded limiting closed-cap selector is substituted.

## 2. Three positive defects and their ordinary parts

The body log measures have a subsequential limit

    s_j(-log L_j)_+ eta_j -> s(-log L)_+ eta+a_H,
    0<=a_H<=b,   support(a_H) subset Z.               (2)

Here and below the ordinary factors refer to the retained joint selectors. Bounded logarithmic truncations identify the limit off Z; restricting the total limit to Z gives the positive remainder.

For each tilted contact source put

    nu_ij=(sigma_ij/L_ij)rho_ij,
    nu_ij^H=1_(H_j) nu_ij.

Each is bounded by its full row measure. After a subsequence their limiting zero-set parts define

    zeta_i^H=lim(nu_ij^H) restricted_to Z,
    0<=zeta_i^H<=zeta_i.                              (3)

On {L>0} the limiting row is absolutely continuous to ordinary mixed volume; the limiting cap plane is volume-null. Consequently the ordinary part is exactly the row's restriction to H, and

    1_(H_j) grad_X log L_j dm_j
       ->1_H grad_X log L dm+M sum_i c_i zeta_i^H.    (4)

Closed/open choices on the prelimit cap plane agree for these volume measures. At limiting zero points on the cap plane, (3) retains the actual allocation instead of guessing a closed-halfspace bit.

There is a third positive defect. The measures

    (-log L_j)_+ lambda_j

have uniformly bounded mass. Indeed the exact allocated Gauss--Green identity with constant vector tests gives

    u_j integral log L_j d lambda_j
       =integral_boundary s_j log L_j n d eta_j
                             -integral_(K^j intersect H_j) grad_X log L_j dm_j.

The right side is uniformly bounded by the whole surface-log and volume-gradient bounds. Since |u_j|>=b_*, this bounds the signed section-log integral; its positive logarithmic part is bounded by `T_max log(max{1,L_*})`, so its negative part is bounded too.

Thus, after a subsequence,

    (-log L_j)_+ lambda_j ->(-log L)_+ lambda+s_H,
    s_H>=0,   support(s_H) subset Z.                 (5)

The ordinary section logarithm is integrable. Each positive-dimensional proper section or supporting facet is a fixed convex (d−1)-body on which the finite concave L is positive in relative interior; it cannot vanish identically there because its zero faces have dimension at most d−2. Concavity gives the usual integrable logarithmic distance-to-boundary bound. Lower-dimensional sections have zero coarea. The d=1 case is a point with strictly positive limiting L. These observations also give lambda(Z)=0, so the same truncation argument as for (2) identifies the nonnegative residual (5).

## 3. Exact capwise flux and complementary cancellation

For every test phi(z,X) that is C1 in X, the prelimit allocated identity is

    integral_boundary s_j phi log L_j n d eta_j
      =integral_(H_j) [log L_j grad_X phi
                                    +phi grad_X log L_j] dm_j
                         +u_j integral phi log L_j d lambda_j. (6)

It is the ordinary cap divergence formula in a proper fiber. For an inside supporting facet its body and section selectors sum to one; for an outside supporting facet their equal contributions cancel on moving the section term to the left. Therefore (6) holds for all the retained statuses.

The bulk log term has no defect by the already proved uniform integrability of log L_j. Use (2), (4), and (5), then subtract the limiting-body allocated Gauss--Green formula. The result is the vector-measure identity

    -pi_*(n a_H)=M sum_i c_i zeta_i^H-u s_H.           (7)

The projection pi forgets the normal coordinate only. Both terms on the right are measures on the physical sampled set. Equation (7) extends from C1 to continuous physical tests by density. It does not assign a normal to the volume or section defects.

For the complementary cap choose the complementary body selector 1−s_j and the SAME allocated section measure. Then

    a_H+a_(H^c)=b,
    zeta_i^H+zeta_i^(H^c)=zeta_i,
    s_(H^c)=s_H.                                     (8)

The complementary continuous normal is −u. Adding its formula (7) cancels the section defect exactly and recovers (1). This is why the full-body flux by itself does not reveal a possibly nonzero section defect.

## 4. No section defect on a uniformly interior contact fiber

Fix one sampled base p. Suppose the current cap section in K_p^j contains a relative (d−1)-ball of fixed radius, and contains a point Y'_j where `L_j(Y'_j)>=l>0`. Keep the common diameter and parameter-maximum bounds. Then

    s_H restricted_to base p =0.                      (9)

Here is a direct uniform-integrability proof. On the section D_j, concavity and its diameter bound give

    L_j(X)>=l dist_(D_j)(X,boundary D_j)/(2R).

For convex section bodies with a uniform inball and outer bound, their intrinsic boundary collars have volume at most C t. Hence, for large A,

    |{X in D_j: -log L_j(X)>A}| <=C' exp(−A),
    integral_{-log L_j>A} (-log L_j) dH_(d−1)
                                    <=C'(A+1)exp(−A).

This proves uniform integrability, and the moving-section compactness identifies the ordinary limit. Bounded coarea factors do not change it. In d=1 the section is a point whose parameter is uniformly positive, so the conclusion is immediate.

In the selected buffered application, an assigned contact mark Y_j has an own ball and `L_j(Y_j)>=l_*`. Its plane is only a vanishing physical buffer away. Project Y_j onto the cap plane. Bounded plane slopes, `|u_j|>=b_*`, and uniformly bounded PL gradients give a section point Y'_j with `L_j(Y'_j)>=l_*/2`, and the section contains a fixed ball. Therefore (9) holds on EVERY assigned contact fiber of that record. Any remaining s_H is confined to other sampled bases.

## 5. Directional consequence with the cap-load budget

For a finite retained cap law with weights theta_H, define

    a=sum_H theta_H a_H,
    zeta_i^cap=sum_H theta_H zeta_i^H.

Summing (7) gives the exact cap-load defect flux

    -pi_*(n a)=M sum_i c_i zeta_i^cap
                                  -sum_H theta_H u_H s_H. (10)

This identity supplements, rather than replaces, the root cap-load constraint

    integral psi(n) f(w) d(a+q)
                    <=beta integral psi(n) f(w) db,

where q>=0 is the retained quadratic-log reserve, psi>=0 is continuous, and f is nonnegative convex. In particular, using psi(n)=|e.n| and f=1 in that constraint, and applying the triangle inequality separately to (7), gives

    sum_H theta_H |e.u_H| s_H(total)
      <=beta integral |e.n| db-integral |e.n| dq
                       +M sum_i |e.c_i| zeta_i^cap(S).  (11)

All masses and directions in (10)–(11) are actual joint limits. The last term has no asserted sign cancellation, and the section defects are not independent of the cap geometry. These are genuine directional restrictions, but they do not force b or zeta to vanish. In particular replacing (7) by the full-body formula with only a_H and zeta_i^H would omit the necessary section term.

## 6. Exact nonzero section correction on the truncated triangles

Use Slab's actual sequence

    K_m={x,y>=0:a<=x+y<=1},
    a=1/m, eta=2^(−m), L_m=c_m(x+y−a+eta),
    c_m->c=exp(1/2), M->1/2.

The whole defects are

    b=sqrt(2)log2 delta_(n_0,0), n_0=−(1,1)/sqrt(2),
    zeta=2c^(−1)log2 delta_0,
    c_source=c(1,1).

Take the INSIDE supporting cap `x+y>=a`, with body allocation zero on its bottom facet and section allocation one. Its captured volume is all K_m. The bottom section's coarea is a, and its negative-log weighted coarea tends to log2. Thus

    a_H=0, zeta^H=zeta, s_H=log2 delta_0, u=(1,1).

Both terms on the right of (7) are `(log2,log2)delta_0`, and cancel. Omitting s_H would be false.

For comparison take the proper cap `x−y>=0`, whose plane passes through the uniformly interior contact source. Symmetry gives `zeta^H=zeta/2` and `a_H=b/2`. Its section-log integral has only the ordinary limit, since the one-dimensional logarithmic primitive has lower endpoint `eta log eta ->0`; equivalently Section 4 applies. Hence `s_H=0`, and (7) is exactly half the whole-body identity. These calibrations are not asserted to be a globally critical or deepest-source cap family.
